### What expiry
**The third expiry out**, whatever weekday it falls on. NVDA lists Mon/Wed/Fri, so the
third is always about a week away and the book holds a rotation of dates.

| write on | third expiry lands | days |
|---|---|---|
| Monday | next Monday | 7 |
| Wednesday | next Wednesday | 7 |
| Friday | next Friday | 7 |

> Replaces "the first Friday at least 5 days out", which sounds equivalent and is not:
> from a Monday that jumped to a Friday eleven days out, so the tenor swung between 7
> and 11 days by weekday. Measured under the live 15-contract cap:
>
> | expiry | tenor | premium/yr | avg price paid |
> |---|---|---|---|
> | nearest Friday | 4d | $610,986 | -1.8% vs market |
> | **3 expiries out** | 7d | **$879,322** | **-3.3%** |
> | 4 expiries out | 10d | $764,975 | -3.7% |
>
> Better on premium and on entry price at once. Four out buys slightly cheaper but
> gives back $114k, because longer contracts sit in the 15-contract cap and stop you
> writing.
>
> Every slice must get a full week. Slicing into the same near expiry was measured and
> fails: the late-week writes are one and two day contracts paying almost nothing.

| Friday | next Friday | 7 |

> Replaces "the first Friday at least 5 days out", which sounds equivalent and is not:
> from a Monday that jumped to a Friday eleven days out, so the tenor swung between 7
> and 11 days by weekday. Measured under the live 15-contract cap:
>
> | expiry | tenor | premium/yr | avg price paid |
> |---|---|---|---|
> | nearest Friday | 4d | $610,986 | -1.8% vs market |
> | **3 expiries out** | 7d | **$879,322** | **-3.3%** |
> | 4 expiries out | 10d | $764,975 | -3.7% |
>
> Better on premium and on entry price at once. Four out buys slightly cheaper but
> gives back $114k, because longer contracts sit in the 15-contract cap and stop you
> writing.
>
> Every slice must get a full week. Slicing into the same near expiry was measured and
> fails: the late-week writes are one and two day contracts paying almost nothing.

>
> | expiry | tenor | premium/yr | avg price paid |
> |---|---|---|---|
> | nearest Friday | 4d | $610,986 | -1.8% vs market |
> | **3 expiries out** | 7d | **$879,322** | **-3.3%** |
> | 4 expiries out | 10d | $764,975 | -3.7% |
>
> Better on premium and on entry price at once. Four out buys slightly cheaper but
> gives back $114k, because longer contracts sit in the 15-contract cap and stop you
> writing.
>
> Every slice must get a full week. Slicing into the same near expiry was measured and
> fails: the late-week writes are one and two day contracts paying almost nothing.

> gives back $114k, because longer contracts sit in the 15-contract cap and stop you
> writing.

> fails: the late-week writes are one and two day contracts paying almost nothing.

third is always about a week away and the book holds a rotation of dates.

| write on | third expiry lands | days |
|---|---|---|
| Monday | next Monday | 7 |
| Wednesday | next Wednesday | 7 |
| Friday | next Friday | 7 |

> Replaces "the first Friday at least 5 days out", which sounds equivalent and is not:
> from a Monday that jumped to a Friday eleven days out, so the tenor swung between 7
> and 11 days by weekday. Measured under the live 15-contract cap:
>
> | expiry | tenor | premium/yr | avg price paid |
> |---|---|---|---|
> | nearest Friday | 4d | $610,986 | -1.8% vs market |
> | **3 expiries out** | 7d | **$879,322** | **-3.3%** |
> | 4 expiries out | 10d | $764,975 | -3.7% |
>
> Better on premium and on entry price at once. Four out buys slightly cheaper but
> gives back $114k, because longer contracts sit in the 15-contract cap and stop you
> writing.
>
> Every slice must get a full week. Slicing into the same near expiry was measured and
> fails: the late-week writes are one and two day contracts paying almost nothing.

| Friday | next Friday | 7 |

> Replaces "the first Friday at least 5 days out", which sounds equivalent and is not:
> from a Monday that jumped to a Friday eleven days out, so the tenor swung between 7
> and 11 days by weekday. Measured under the live 15-contract cap:
>
> | expiry | tenor | premium/yr | avg price paid |
> |---|---|---|---|
> | nearest Friday | 4d | $610,986 | -1.8% vs market |
> | **3 expiries out** | 7d | **$879,322** | **-3.3%** |
> | 4 expiries out | 10d | $764,975 | -3.7% |
>
> Better on premium and on entry price at once. Four out buys slightly cheaper but
> gives back $114k, because longer contracts sit in the 15-contract cap and stop you
> writing.
>
> Every slice must get a full week. Slicing into the same near expiry was measured and
> fails: the late-week writes are one and two day contracts paying almost nothing.

>
> | expiry | tenor | premium/yr | avg price paid |
> |---|---|---|---|
> | nearest Friday | 4d | $610,986 | -1.8% vs market |
> | **3 expiries out** | 7d | **$879,322** | **-3.3%** |
> | 4 expiries out | 10d | $764,975 | -3.7% |
>
> Better on premium and on entry price at once. Four out buys slightly cheaper but
> gives back $114k, because longer contracts sit in the 15-contract cap and stop you
> writing.
>
> Every slice must get a full week. Slicing into the same near expiry was measured and
> fails: the late-week writes are one and two day contracts paying almost nothing.

**The third expiry out**, whatever weekday it falls on. NVDA lists Mon/Wed/Fri, so the

>
> Better on premium and on entry price at once. Four out buys slightly cheaper but
> gives back $114k, because longer contracts sit in the 15-contract cap and stop you
> writing.
>
> Every slice must get a full week. Slicing into the same near expiry was measured and
> fails: the late-week writes are one and two day contracts paying almost nothing.

s### What expiry
**The third expiry out**, whatever weekday it falls on. NVDA lists Mon/Wed/Fri, so the
third is always about a week away and the book holds a rotation of dates.

| write on | third expiry lands | days |
|---|---|---|
| Monday | next Monday | 7 |
| Wednesday | next Wednesday | 7 |
| Friday | next Friday | 7 |

> Replaces "the first Friday at least 5 days out", which sounds equivalent and is not:
> from a Monday that jumped to a Friday eleven days out, so the tenor swung between 7
> and 11 days by weekday. Measured under the live 15-contract cap:
>
> | expiry | tenor | premium/yr | avg price paid |
> |---|---|---|---|
> | nearest Friday | 4d | $610,986 | -1.8% vs market |
> | **3 expiries out** | 7d | **$879,322** | **-3.3%** |
> | 4 expiries out | 10d | $764,975 | -3.7% |
>
> Better on premium and on entry price at once. Four out buys slightly cheaper but
> gives back $114k, because longer contracts sit in the 15-contract cap and stop you
> writing.
>
> Every slice must get a full week. Slicing into the same near expiry was measured and
> fails: the late-week writes are one and two day contracts paying almost nothing.

third is always about a week away and the book holds a rotation of dates.

| write on | third expiry lands | days |
|---|---|---|
| Monday | next Monday | 7 |
| Wednesday | next Wednesday | 7 |
| Friday | next Friday | 7 |

> Replaces "the first Friday at least 5 days out", which sounds equivalent and is not:
> from a Monday that jumped to a Friday eleven days out, so the tenor swung between 7
> and 11 days by weekday. Measured under the live 15-contract cap:
>
> | expiry | tenor | premium/yr | avg price paid |
> |---|---|---|---|
> | nearest Friday | 4d | $610,986 | -1.8% vs market |
> | **3 expiries out** | 7d | **$879,322** | **-3.3%** |
> | 4 expiries out | 10d | $764,975 | -3.7% |
>
> Better on premium and on entry price at once. Four out buys slightly cheaper but
> gives back $114k, because longer contracts sit in the 15-contract cap and stop you
> writing.
>
> Every slice must get a full week. Slicing into the same near expiry was measured and
> fails: the late-week writes are one and two day contracts paying almost nothing.

| Friday | next Friday | 7 |

> Replaces "the first Friday at least 5 days out", which sounds equivalent and is not:
> from a Monday that jumped to a Friday eleven days out, so the tenor swung between 7
> and 11 days by weekday. Measured under the live 15-contract cap:
>
> | expiry | tenor | premium/yr | avg price paid |
> |---|---|---|---|
> | nearest Friday | 4d | $610,986 | -1.8% vs market |
> | **3 expiries out** | 7d | **$879,322** | **-3.3%** |
> | 4 expiries out | 10d | $764,975 | -3.7% |
>
> Better on premium and on entry price at once. Four out buys slightly cheaper but
> gives back $114k, because longer contracts sit in the 15-contract cap and stop you
> writing.
>
> Every slice must get a full week. Slicing into the same near expiry was measured and
> fails: the late-week writes are one and two day contracts paying almost nothing.

> | **3 expiries out** | 7d | **$879,322** | **-3.3%** |
> | 4 expiries out | 10d | $764,975 | -3.7% |

> Better on premium and on entry price at once. Four out buys slightly cheaper but
> gives back $114k, because longer contracts sit in the 15-contract cap and stop you
> writing.
>
> Every slice must get a full week. Slicing into the same near expiry was measured and
> fails: the late-week writes are one and two day contracts paying almost nothing.

e### What expiry
**The third expiry out**, whatever weekday it falls on. NVDA lists Mon/Wed/Fri, so the
third is always about a week away and the book holds a rotation of dates.

| write on | third expiry lands | days |
|---|---|---|
| Monday | next Monday | 7 |
| Wednesday | next Wednesday | 7 |
| Friday | next Friday | 7 |

> Replaces "the first Friday at least 5 days out", which sounds equivalent and is not:
> from a Monday that jumped to a Friday eleven days out, so the tenor swung between 7
> and 11 days by weekday. Measured under the live 15-contract cap:
>
> | expiry | tenor | premium/yr | avg price paid |
> |---|---|---|---|
> | nearest Friday | 4d | $610,986 | -1.8% vs market |
> | **3 expiries out** | 7d | **$879,322** | **-3.3%** |
> | 4 expiries out | 10d | $764,975 | -3.7% |
>
> Better on premium and on entry price at once. Four out buys slightly cheaper but
> gives back $114k, because longer contracts sit in the 15-contract cap and stop you
> writing.
>
> Every slice must get a full week. Slicing into the same near expiry was measured and
> fails: the late-week writes are one and two day contracts paying almost nothing.

third is always about a week away and the book holds a rotation of dates.

| write on | third expiry lands | days |
|---|---|---|
| Monday | next Monday | 7 |
| Wednesday | next Wednesday | 7 |
| Friday | next Friday | 7 |

> Replaces "the first Friday at least 5 days out", which sounds equivalent and is not:
> from a Monday that jumped to a Friday eleven days out, so the tenor swung between 7
> and 11 days by weekday. Measured under the live 15-contract cap:
>
> | expiry | tenor | premium/yr | avg price paid |
> |---|---|---|---|
> | nearest Friday | 4d | $610,986 | -1.8% vs market |
> | **3 expiries out** | 7d | **$879,322** | **-3.3%** |
> | 4 expiries out | 10d | $764,975 | -3.7% |
>
> Better on premium and on entry price at once. Four out buys slightly cheaper but
> gives back $114k, because longer contracts sit in the 15-contract cap and stop you
> writing.
>
> Every slice must get a full week. Slicing into the same near expiry was measured and
> fails: the late-week writes are one and two day contracts paying almost nothing.

>

> |---|---|---|---|
> | nearest Friday | 4d | $610,986 | -1.8% vs market |
> | **3 expiries out** | 7d | **$879,322** | **-3.3%** |
> | 4 expiries out | 10d | $764,975 | -3.7% |
>
> Better on premium and on entry price at once. Four out buys slightly cheaper but
> gives back $114k, because longer contracts sit in the 15-contract cap and stop you
> writing.

> fails: the late-week writes are one and two day contracts paying almost nothing.

> | expiry | tenor | premium/yr | avg price paid |
> |---|---|---|---|
> | nearest Friday | 4d | $610,986 | -1.8% vs market |
> | **3 expiries out** | 7d | **$879,322** | **-3.3%** |
> | 4 expiries out | 10d | $764,975 | -3.7% |
>
> Better on premium and on entry price at once. Four out buys slightly cheaper but
> gives back $114k, because longer contracts sit in the 15-contract cap and stop you
> writing.
>
> Every slice must get a full week. Slicing into the same near expiry was measured and
> fails: the late-week writes are one and two day contracts paying almost nothing.

h### What expiry
**The third expiry out**, whatever weekday it falls on. NVDA lists Mon/Wed/Fri, so the
third is always about a week away and the book holds a rotation of dates.

| write on | third expiry lands | days |
|---|---|---|
| Monday | next Monday | 7 |
| Wednesday | next Wednesday | 7 |
| Friday | next Friday | 7 |

> Replaces "the first Friday at least 5 days out", which sounds equivalent and is not:
> from a Monday that jumped to a Friday eleven days out, so the tenor swung between 7
> and 11 days by weekday. Measured under the live 15-contract cap:
>
> | expiry | tenor | premium/yr | avg price paid |
> |---|---|---|---|
> | nearest Friday | 4d | $610,986 | -1.8% vs market |
> | **3 expiries out** | 7d | **$879,322** | **-3.3%** |
> | 4 expiries out | 10d | $764,975 | -3.7% |
>
> Better on premium and on entry price at once. Four out buys slightly cheaper but
> gives back $114k, because longer contracts sit in the 15-contract cap and stop you
> writing.
>
> Every slice must get a full week. Slicing into the same near expiry was measured and
> fails: the late-week writes are one and two day contracts paying almost nothing.

third is always about a week away and the book holds a rotation of dates.

| write on | third expiry lands | days |
|---|---|---|
| Monday | next Monday | 7 |
| Wednesday | next Wednesday | 7 |
| Friday | next Friday | 7 |

> Replaces "the first Friday at least 5 days out", which sounds equivalent and is not:
> from a Monday that jumped to a Friday eleven days out, so the tenor swung between 7
> and 11 days by weekday. Measured under the live 15-contract cap:
>
> | expiry | tenor | premium/yr | avg price paid |
> |---|---|---|---|
> | nearest Friday | 4d | $610,986 | -1.8% vs market |
> | **3 expiries out** | 7d | **$879,322** | **-3.3%** |
> | 4 expiries out | 10d | $764,975 | -3.7% |
>
> Better on premium and on entry price at once. Four out buys slightly cheaper but
> gives back $114k, because longer contracts sit in the 15-contract cap and stop you
> writing.
>
> Every slice must get a full week. Slicing into the same near expiry was measured and
> fails: the late-week writes are one and two day contracts paying almost nothing.

| Friday | next Friday | 7 |

> Replaces "the first Friday at least 5 days out", which sounds equivalent and is not:
> from a Monday that jumped to a Friday eleven days out, so the tenor swung between 7
> and 11 days by weekday. Measured under the live 15-contract cap:
>
> | expiry | tenor | premium/yr | avg price paid |
> |---|---|---|---|
> | nearest Friday | 4d | $610,986 | -1.8% vs market |
> | **3 expiries out** | 7d | **$879,322** | **-3.3%** |
> | 4 expiries out | 10d | $764,975 | -3.7% |
>
> Better on premium and on entry price at once. Four out buys slightly cheaper but
> gives back $114k, because longer contracts sit in the 15-contract cap and stop you
> writing.
>
> Every slice must get a full week. Slicing into the same near expiry was measured and
> fails: the late-week writes are one and two day contracts paying almost nothing.

>
> | expiry | tenor | premium/yr | avg price paid |
> |---|---|---|---|
> | nearest Friday | 4d | $610,986 | -1.8% vs market |
> | **3 expiries out** | 7d | **$879,322** | **-3.3%** |
> | 4 expiries out | 10d | $764,975 | -3.7% |
>
> Better on premium and on entry price at once. Four out buys slightly cheaper but
> gives back $114k, because longer contracts sit in the 15-contract cap and stop you
> writing.
>
> Every slice must get a full week. Slicing into the same near expiry was measured and
> fails: the late-week writes are one and two day contracts paying almost nothing.

third is always about a week away and the book holds a rotation of dates.

| write on | third expiry lands | days |
|---|---|---|
| Monday | next Monday | 7 |
| Wednesday | next Wednesday | 7 |
| Friday | next Friday | 7 |

> Replaces "the first Friday at least 5 days out", which sounds equivalent and is not:
> from a Monday that jumped to a Friday eleven days out, so the tenor swung between 7
> and 11 days by weekday. Measured under the live 15-contract cap:
>
> | expiry | tenor | premium/yr | avg price paid |
> |---|---|---|---|
> | nearest Friday | 4d | $610,986 | -1.8% vs market |
> | **3 expiries out** | 7d | **$879,322** | **-3.3%** |
> | 4 expiries out | 10d | $764,975 | -3.7% |
>
> Better on premium and on entry price at once. Four out buys slightly cheaper but
> gives back $114k, because longer contracts sit in the 15-contract cap and stop you
> writing.
>
> Every slice must get a full week. Slicing into the same near expiry was measured and
> fails: the late-week writes are one and two day contracts paying almost nothing.

| Friday | next Friday | 7 |

> Replaces "the first Friday at least 5 days out", which sounds equivalent and is not:
> from a Monday that jumped to a Friday eleven days out, so the tenor swung between 7
> and 11 days by weekday. Measured under the live 15-contract cap:
>
> | expiry | tenor | premium/yr | avg price paid |
> |---|---|---|---|
> | nearest Friday | 4d | $610,986 | -1.8% vs market |
> | **3 expiries out** | 7d | **$879,322** | **-3.3%** |
> | 4 expiries out | 10d | $764,975 | -3.7% |
>
> Better on premium and on entry price at once. Four out buys slightly cheaper but
> gives back $114k, because longer contracts sit in the 15-contract cap and stop you
> writing.
>
> Every slice must get a full week. Slicing into the same near expiry was measured and
> fails: the late-week writes are one and two day contracts paying almost nothing.

>
> | expiry | tenor | premium/yr | avg price paid |
> |---|---|---|---|
> | nearest Friday | 4d | $610,986 | -1.8% vs market |
> | **3 expiries out** | 7d | **$879,322** | **-3.3%** |
> | 4 expiries out | 10d | $764,975 | -3.7% |
>
> Better on premium and on entry price at once. Four out buys slightly cheaper but
> gives back $114k, because longer contracts sit in the 15-contract cap and stop you
> writing.
>
> Every slice must get a full week. Slicing into the same near expiry was measured and
> fails: the late-week writes are one and two day contracts paying almost nothing.

**The third expiry out**, whatever weekday it falls on. NVDA lists Mon/Wed/Fri, so the
third is always about a week away and the book holds a rotation of dates.

| write on | third expiry lands | days |
|---|---|---|
| Monday | next Monday | 7 |
| Wednesday | next Wednesday | 7 |
| Friday | next Friday | 7 |

> Replaces "the first Friday at least 5 days out", which sounds equivalent and is not:
> from a Monday that jumped to a Friday eleven days out, so the tenor swung between 7
> and 11 days by weekday. Measured under the live 15-contract cap:
>
> | expiry | tenor | premium/yr | avg price paid |
> |---|---|---|---|
> | nearest Friday | 4d | $610,986 | -1.8% vs market |
> | **3 expiries out** | 7d | **$879,322** | **-3.3%** |
> | 4 expiries out | 10d | $764,975 | -3.7% |
>
> Better on premium and on entry price at once. Four out buys slightly cheaper but
> gives back $114k, because longer contracts sit in the 15-contract cap and stop you
> writing.
>
> Every slice must get a full week. Slicing into the same near expiry was measured and
> fails: the late-week writes are one and two day contracts paying almost nothing.

third is always about a week away and the book holds a rotation of dates.

| write on | third expiry lands | days |
|---|---|---|
| Monday | next Monday | 7 |
| Wednesday | next Wednesday | 7 |
| Friday | next Friday | 7 |

> Replaces "the first Friday at least 5 days out", which sounds equivalent and is not:
> from a Monday that jumped to a Friday eleven days out, so the tenor swung between 7
> and 11 days by weekday. Measured under the live 15-contract cap:
>
> | expiry | tenor | premium/yr | avg price paid |
> |---|---|---|---|
> | nearest Friday | 4d | $610,986 | -1.8% vs market |
> | **3 expiries out** | 7d | **$879,322** | **-3.3%** |
> | 4 expiries out | 10d | $764,975 | -3.7% |
>
> Better on premium and on entry price at once. Four out buys slightly cheaper but
> gives back $114k, because longer contracts sit in the 15-contract cap and stop you
> writing.
>
> Every slice must get a full week. Slicing into the same near expiry was measured and
> fails: the late-week writes are one and two day contracts paying almost nothing.

| Friday | next Friday | 7 |

> Replaces "the first Friday at least 5 days out", which sounds equivalent and is not:
> from a Monday that jumped to a Friday eleven days out, so the tenor swung between 7
> and 11 days by weekday. Measured under the live 15-contract cap:
>
> | expiry | tenor | premium/yr | avg price paid |
> |---|---|---|---|
> | nearest Friday | 4d | $610,986 | -1.8% vs market |
> | **3 expiries out** | 7d | **$879,322** | **-3.3%** |
> | 4 expiries out | 10d | $764,975 | -3.7% |
>
> Better on premium and on entry price at once. Four out buys slightly cheaper but
> gives back $114k, because longer contracts sit in the 15-contract cap and stop you
> writing.
>
> Every slice must get a full week. Slicing into the same near expiry was measured and
> fails: the late-week writes are one and two day contracts paying almost nothing.

> writing.

6### What expiry
**The third expiry out**, whatever weekday it falls on. NVDA lists Mon/Wed/Fri, so the
third is always about a week away and the book holds a rotation of dates.

| write on | third expiry lands | days |
|---|---|---|
| Monday | next Monday | 7 |
| Wednesday | next Wednesday | 7 |
| Friday | next Friday | 7 |

> Replaces "the first Friday at least 5 days out", which sounds equivalent and is not:
> from a Monday that jumped to a Friday eleven days out, so the tenor swung between 7
> and 11 days by weekday. Measured under the live 15-contract cap:
>
> | expiry | tenor | premium/yr | avg price paid |
> |---|---|---|---|
> | nearest Friday | 4d | $610,986 | -1.8% vs market |
> | **3 expiries out** | 7d | **$879,322** | **-3.3%** |
> | 4 expiries out | 10d | $764,975 | -3.7% |
>
> Better on premium and on entry price at once. Four out buys slightly cheaper but
> gives back $114k, because longer contracts sit in the 15-contract cap and stop you
> writing.
>
> Every slice must get a full week. Slicing into the same near expiry was measured and
> fails: the late-week writes are one and two day contracts paying almost nothing.

third is always about a week away and the book holds a rotation of dates.

| write on | third expiry lands | days |
|---|---|---|
| Monday | next Monday | 7 |
| Wednesday | next Wednesday | 7 |
| Friday | next Friday | 7 |

> Replaces "the first Friday at least 5 days out", which sounds equivalent and is not:
> from a Monday that jumped to a Friday eleven days out, so the tenor swung between 7
> and 11 days by weekday. Measured under the live 15-contract cap:
>
> | expiry | tenor | premium/yr | avg price paid |
> |---|---|---|---|
> | nearest Friday | 4d | $610,986 | -1.8% vs market |
> | **3 expiries out** | 7d | **$879,322** | **-3.3%** |
> | 4 expiries out | 10d | $764,975 | -3.7% |
>
> Better on premium and on entry price at once. Four out buys slightly cheaper but
> gives back $114k, because longer contracts sit in the 15-contract cap and stop you
> writing.
>
> Every slice must get a full week. Slicing into the same near expiry was measured and
> fails: the late-week writes are one and two day contracts paying almost nothing.

| Friday | next Friday | 7 |

> from a Monday that jumped to a Friday eleven days out, so the tenor swung between 7
> and 11 days by weekday. Measured under the live 15-contract cap:
>
> | expiry | tenor | premium/yr | avg price paid |
> |---|---|---|---|
> | nearest Friday | 4d | $610,986 | -1.8% vs market |
> | **3 expiries out** | 7d | **$879,322** | **-3.3%** |
> | 4 expiries out | 10d | $764,975 | -3.7% |
>
> Better on premium and on entry price at once. Four out buys slightly cheaper but
> gives back $114k, because longer contracts sit in the 15-contract cap and stop you
> writing.
>
> Every slice must get a full week. Slicing into the same near expiry was measured and
> fails: the late-week writes are one and two day contracts paying almost nothing.

>
> | expiry | tenor | premium/yr | avg price paid |
> |---|---|---|---|
> | nearest Friday | 4d | $610,986 | -1.8% vs market |
> | **3 expiries out** | 7d | **$879,322** | **-3.3%** |
> | 4 expiries out | 10d | $764,975 | -3.7% |
>
> Better on premium and on entry price at once. Four out buys slightly cheaper but
> gives back $114k, because longer contracts sit in the 15-contract cap and stop you
> writing.
>
> Every slice must get a full week. Slicing into the same near expiry was measured and
> fails: the late-week writes are one and two day contracts paying almost nothing.

**The third expiry out**, whatever weekday it falls on. NVDA lists Mon/Wed/Fri, so the
third is always about a week away and the book holds a rotation of dates.

| write on | third expiry lands | days |
|---|---|---|
| Monday | next Monday | 7 |
| Wednesday | next Wednesday | 7 |
| Friday | next Friday | 7 |

> Replaces "the first Friday at least 5 days out", which sounds equivalent and is not:
> from a Monday that jumped to a Friday eleven days out, so the tenor swung between 7
> and 11 days by weekday. Measured under the live 15-contract cap:
>
> | expiry | tenor | premium/yr | avg price paid |
> |---|---|---|---|

> | **3 expiries out** | 7d | **$879,322** | **-3.3%** |
> | 4 expiries out | 10d | $764,975 | -3.7% |
>
> Better on premium and on entry price at once. Four out buys slightly cheaper but
> gives back $114k, because longer contracts sit in the 15-contract cap and stop you
> writing.
>
> Every slice must get a full week. Slicing into the same near expiry was measured and
> fails: the late-week writes are one and two day contracts paying almost nothing.

third is always about a week away and the book holds a rotation of dates.

| write on | third expiry lands | days |
|---|---|---|
| Monday | next Monday | 7 |
| Wednesday | next Wednesday | 7 |
| Friday | next Friday | 7 |

> Replaces "the first Friday at least 5 days out", which sounds equivalent and is not:
> from a Monday that jumped to a Friday eleven days out, so the tenor swung between 7
> and 11 days by weekday. Measured under the live 15-contract cap:
>
> | expiry | tenor | premium/yr | avg price paid |
> |---|---|---|---|
> | nearest Friday | 4d | $610,986 | -1.8% vs market |
> | **3 expiries out** | 7d | **$879,322** | **-3.3%** |
> | 4 expiries out | 10d | $764,975 | -3.7% |
>
> Better on premium and on entry price at once. Four out buys slightly cheaper but
> gives back $114k, because longer contracts sit in the 15-contract cap and stop you
> writing.
>
> Every slice must get a full week. Slicing into the same near expiry was measured and
> fails: the late-week writes are one and two day contracts paying almost nothing.

| Friday | next Friday | 7 |

> Replaces "the first Friday at least 5 days out", which sounds equivalent and is not:
> from a Monday that jumped to a Friday eleven days out, so the tenor swung between 7
> and 11 days by weekday. Measured under the live 15-contract cap:
>
> | expiry | tenor | premium/yr | avg price paid |
> |---|---|---|---|
> | nearest Friday | 4d | $610,986 | -1.8% vs market |
> | **3 expiries out** | 7d | **$879,322** | **-3.3%** |
> | 4 expiries out | 10d | $764,975 | -3.7% |
>
> Better on premium and on entry price at once. Four out buys slightly cheaper but
> gives back $114k, because longer contracts sit in the 15-contract cap and stop you
> writing.
>
> Every slice must get a full week. Slicing into the same near expiry was measured and
> fails: the late-week writes are one and two day contracts paying almost nothing.

> | **3 expiries out** | 7d | **$879,322** | **-3.3%** |
> | 4 expiries out | 10d | $764,975 | -3.7% |

> Better on premium and on entry price at once. Four out buys slightly cheaper but
> gives back $114k, because longer contracts sit in the 15-contract cap and stop you
> writing.

> Every slice must get a full week. Slicing into the same near expiry was measured and
> fails: the late-week writes are one and two day contracts paying almost nothing.

**The third expiry out**, whatever weekday it falls on. NVDA lists Mon/Wed/Fri, so the
third is always about a week away and the book holds a rotation of dates.

| write on | third expiry lands | days |
|---|---|---|
| Monday | next Monday | 7 |
| Wednesday | next Wednesday | 7 |
| Friday | next Friday | 7 |

> Replaces "the first Friday at least 5 days out", which sounds equivalent and is not:
> from a Monday that jumped to a Friday eleven days out, so the tenor swung between 7
> and 11 days by weekday. Measured under the live 15-contract cap:
>
> | expiry | tenor | premium/yr | avg price paid |
> |---|---|---|---|
> | nearest Friday | 4d | $610,986 | -1.8% vs market |
> | **3 expiries out** | 7d | **$879,322** | **-3.3%** |
> | 4 expiries out | 10d | $764,975 | -3.7% |
>
> Better on premium and on entry price at once. Four out buys slightly cheaper but
> gives back $114k, because longer contracts sit in the 15-contract cap and stop you
> writing.
>
> Every slice must get a full week. Slicing into the same near expiry was measured and
> fails: the late-week writes are one and two day contracts paying almost nothing.

third is always about a week away and the book holds a rotation of dates.

| write on | third expiry lands | days |
|---|---|---|
| Monday | next Monday | 7 |
| Wednesday | next Wednesday | 7 |
| Friday | next Friday | 7 |

> Replaces "the first Friday at least 5 days out", which sounds equivalent and is not:
> from a Monday that jumped to a Friday eleven days out, so the tenor swung between 7
> and 11 days by weekday. Measured under the live 15-contract cap:
>
> | expiry | tenor | premium/yr | avg price paid |
> |---|---|---|---|
> | nearest Friday | 4d | $610,986 | -1.8% vs market |
> | **3 expiries out** | 7d | **$879,322** | **-3.3%** |
> | 4 expiries out | 10d | $764,975 | -3.7% |
>
> Better on premium and on entry price at once. Four out buys slightly cheaper but
> gives back $114k, because longer contracts sit in the 15-contract cap and stop you
> writing.
>
> Every slice must get a full week. Slicing into the same near expiry was measured and
> fails: the late-week writes are one and two day contracts paying almost nothing.

| Friday | next Friday | 7 |

> Replaces "the first Friday at least 5 days out", which sounds equivalent and is not:
> from a Monday that jumped to a Friday eleven days out, so the tenor swung between 7
> and 11 days by weekday. Measured under the live 15-contract cap:
>
> | expiry | tenor | premium/yr | avg price paid |
> |---|---|---|---|
> | nearest Friday | 4d | $610,986 | -1.8% vs market |
> | **3 expiries out** | 7d | **$879,322** | **-3.3%** |
> | 4 expiries out | 10d | $764,975 | -3.7% |
>
> Better on premium and on entry price at once. Four out buys slightly cheaper but
> gives back $114k, because longer contracts sit in the 15-contract cap and stop you
> writing.
>
> Every slice must get a full week. Slicing into the same near expiry was measured and
> fails: the late-week writes are one and two day contracts paying almost nothing.

> writing.

> writing.

i### What expiry
**The third expiry out**, whatever weekday it falls on. NVDA lists Mon/Wed/Fri, so the
third is always about a week away and the book holds a rotation of dates.

| write on | third expiry lands | days |
|---|---|---|
| Monday | next Monday | 7 |
| Wednesday | next Wednesday | 7 |
| Friday | next Friday | 7 |

> Replaces "the first Friday at least 5 days out", which sounds equivalent and is not:
> from a Monday that jumped to a Friday eleven days out, so the tenor swung between 7
> and 11 days by weekday. Measured under the live 15-contract cap:
>
> | expiry | tenor | premium/yr | avg price paid |
> |---|---|---|---|
> | nearest Friday | 4d | $610,986 | -1.8% vs market |
> | **3 expiries out** | 7d | **$879,322** | **-3.3%** |
> | 4 expiries out | 10d | $764,975 | -3.7% |
>
> Better on premium and on entry price at once. Four out buys slightly cheaper but
> gives back $114k, because longer contracts sit in the 15-contract cap and stop you
> writing.
>
> Every slice must get a full week. Slicing into the same near expiry was measured and
> fails: the late-week writes are one and two day contracts paying almost nothing.

third is always about a week away and the book holds a rotation of dates.

| write on | third expiry lands | days |
|---|---|---|
| Monday | next Monday | 7 |
| Wednesday | next Wednesday | 7 |
| Friday | next Friday | 7 |

> Replaces "the first Friday at least 5 days out", which sounds equivalent and is not:
> from a Monday that jumped to a Friday eleven days out, so the tenor swung between 7
> and 11 days by weekday. Measured under the live 15-contract cap:
>
> | expiry | tenor | premium/yr | avg price paid |
> |---|---|---|---|
> | nearest Friday | 4d | $610,986 | -1.8% vs market |
> | **3 expiries out** | 7d | **$879,322** | **-3.3%** |
> | 4 expiries out | 10d | $764,975 | -3.7% |
>
> Better on premium and on entry price at once. Four out buys slightly cheaper but
> gives back $114k, because longer contracts sit in the 15-contract cap and stop you
> writing.
>
> Every slice must get a full week. Slicing into the same near expiry was measured and
> fails: the late-week writes are one and two day contracts paying almost nothing.

| Friday | next Friday | 7 |

> Replaces "the first Friday at least 5 days out", which sounds equivalent and is not:
> from a Monday that jumped to a Friday eleven days out, so the tenor swung between 7
> and 11 days by weekday. Measured under the live 15-contract cap:
>
> | expiry | tenor | premium/yr | avg price paid |
> |---|---|---|---|
> | nearest Friday | 4d | $610,986 | -1.8% vs market |
> | **3 expiries out** | 7d | **$879,322** | **-3.3%** |
> | 4 expiries out | 10d | $764,975 | -3.7% |
>
> Better on premium and on entry price at once. Four out buys slightly cheaper but
> gives back $114k, because longer contracts sit in the 15-contract cap and stop you
> writing.
>
> Every slice must get a full week. Slicing into the same near expiry was measured and
> fails: the late-week writes are one and two day contracts paying almost nothing.

> | **3 expiries out** | 7d | **$879,322** | **-3.3%** |
> | 4 expiries out | 10d | $764,975 | -3.7% |
>
> Better on premium and on entry price at once. Four out buys slightly cheaper but
> gives back $114k, because longer contracts sit in the 15-contract cap and stop you
> writing.
>
> Every slice must get a full week. Slicing into the same near expiry was measured and
> fails: the late-week writes are one and two day contracts paying almost nothing.

**The third expiry out**, whatever weekday it falls on. NVDA lists Mon/Wed/Fri, so the
third is always about a week away and the book holds a rotation of dates.

| write on | third expiry lands | days |
|---|---|---|
| Monday | next Monday | 7 |
| Wednesday | next Wednesday | 7 |
| Friday | next Friday | 7 |

> Replaces "the first Friday at least 5 days out", which sounds equivalent and is not:
> from a Monday that jumped to a Friday eleven days out, so the tenor swung between 7
> and 11 days by weekday. Measured under the live 15-contract cap:
>
> | expiry | tenor | premium/yr | avg price paid |
> |---|---|---|---|
> | nearest Friday | 4d | $610,986 | -1.8% vs market |
> | **3 expiries out** | 7d | **$879,322** | **-3.3%** |
> | 4 expiries out | 10d | $764,975 | -3.7% |
>
> Better on premium and on entry price at once. Four out buys slightly cheaper but
> gives back $114k, because longer contracts sit in the 15-contract cap and stop you
> writing.
>
> Every slice must get a full week. Slicing into the same near expiry was measured and
> fails: the late-week writes are one and two day contracts paying almost nothing.

third is always about a week away and the book holds a rotation of dates.

| write on | third expiry lands | days |
|---|---|---|
| Monday | next Monday | 7 |
| Wednesday | next Wednesday | 7 |
| Friday | next Friday | 7 |

> Replaces "the first Friday at least 5 days out", which sounds equivalent and is not:
> from a Monday that jumped to a Friday eleven days out, so the tenor swung between 7
> and 11 days by weekday. Measured under the live 15-contract cap:
>
> | expiry | tenor | premium/yr | avg price paid |
> |---|---|---|---|
> | nearest Friday | 4d | $610,986 | -1.8% vs market |
> | **3 expiries out** | 7d | **$879,322** | **-3.3%** |
> | 4 expiries out | 10d | $764,975 | -3.7% |
>
> Better on premium and on entry price at once. Four out buys slightly cheaper but
> gives back $114k, because longer contracts sit in the 15-contract cap and stop you
> writing.
>
> Every slice must get a full week. Slicing into the same near expiry was measured and
> fails: the late-week writes are one and two day contracts paying almost nothing.

| Friday | next Friday | 7 |

> Replaces "the first Friday at least 5 days out", which sounds equivalent and is not:
> from a Monday that jumped to a Friday eleven days out, so the tenor swung between 7
> and 11 days by weekday. Measured under the live 15-contract cap:
>
> | expiry | tenor | premium/yr | avg price paid |
> |---|---|---|---|
> | nearest Friday | 4d | $610,986 | -1.8% vs market |
> | **3 expiries out** | 7d | **$879,322** | **-3.3%** |
> | 4 expiries out | 10d | $764,975 | -3.7% |
>
> Better on premium and on entry price at once. Four out buys slightly cheaper but
> gives back $114k, because longer contracts sit in the 15-contract cap and stop you
> writing.
>
> Every slice must get a full week. Slicing into the same near expiry was measured and
> fails: the late-week writes are one and two day contracts paying almost nothing.

>
> | expiry | tenor | premium/yr | avg price paid |
> |---|---|---|---|
> | nearest Friday | 4d | $610,986 | -1.8% vs market |
> | **3 expiries out** | 7d | **$879,322** | **-3.3%** |
> | 4 expiries out | 10d | $764,975 | -3.7% |
>
> Better on premium and on entry price at once. Four out buys slightly cheaper but
> gives back $114k, because longer contracts sit in the 15-contract cap and stop you
> writing.
>
> Every slice must get a full week. Slicing into the same near expiry was measured and
> fails: the late-week writes are one and two day contracts paying almost nothing.

**The third expiry out**, whatever weekday it falls on. NVDA lists Mon/Wed/Fri, so the
third is always about a week away and the book holds a rotation of dates.

| write on | third expiry lands | days |
|---|---|---|
| Monday | next Monday | 7 |
| Wednesday | next Wednesday | 7 |
| Friday | next Friday | 7 |

> Replaces "the first Friday at least 5 days out", which sounds equivalent and is not:
> from a Monday that jumped to a Friday eleven days out, so the tenor swung between 7
> and 11 days by weekday. Measured under the live 15-contract cap:
>
> | expiry | tenor | premium/yr | avg price paid |
> |---|---|---|---|

> | **3 expiries out** | 7d | **$879,322** | **-3.3%** |
> | 4 expiries out | 10d | $764,975 | -3.7% |
>
> Better on premium and on entry price at once. Four out buys slightly cheaper but
> gives back $114k, because longer contracts sit in the 15-contract cap and stop you
> writing.
>
> Every slice must get a full week. Slicing into the same near expiry was measured and
> fails: the late-week writes are one and two day contracts paying almost nothing.

third is always about a week away and the book holds a rotation of dates.

| write on | third expiry lands | days |
|---|---|---|
| Monday | next Monday | 7 |
| Wednesday | next Wednesday | 7 |
| Friday | next Friday | 7 |

> Replaces "the first Friday at least 5 days out", which sounds equivalent and is not:
> from a Monday that jumped to a Friday eleven days out, so the tenor swung between 7
> and 11 days by weekday. Measured under the live 15-contract cap:
>
> | expiry | tenor | premium/yr | avg price paid |
> |---|---|---|---|
> | nearest Friday | 4d | $610,986 | -1.8% vs market |
> | **3 expiries out** | 7d | **$879,322** | **-3.3%** |
> | 4 expiries out | 10d | $764,975 | -3.7% |
>
> Better on premium and on entry price at once. Four out buys slightly cheaper but
> gives back $114k, because longer contracts sit in the 15-contract cap and stop you
> writing.
>
> Every slice must get a full week. Slicing into the same near expiry was measured and
> fails: the late-week writes are one and two day contracts paying almost nothing.

| Friday | next Friday | 7 |

> Replaces "the first Friday at least 5 days out", which sounds equivalent and is not:
> from a Monday that jumped to a Friday eleven days out, so the tenor swung between 7
> and 11 days by weekday. Measured under the live 15-contract cap:
>
> | expiry | tenor | premium/yr | avg price paid |
> |---|---|---|---|
> | nearest Friday | 4d | $610,986 | -1.8% vs market |
> | **3 expiries out** | 7d | **$879,322** | **-3.3%** |
> | 4 expiries out | 10d | $764,975 | -3.7% |
>
> Better on premium and on entry price at once. Four out buys slightly cheaper but
> gives back $114k, because longer contracts sit in the 15-contract cap and stop you
> writing.
>
> Every slice must get a full week. Slicing into the same near expiry was measured and
> fails: the late-week writes are one and two day contracts paying almost nothing.

>

> |---|---|---|---|
> | nearest Friday | 4d | $610,986 | -1.8% vs market |
> | **3 expiries out** | 7d | **$879,322** | **-3.3%** |
> | 4 expiries out | 10d | $764,975 | -3.7% |
>
> Better on premium and on entry price at once. Four out buys slightly cheaper but
> gives back $114k, because longer contracts sit in the 15-contract cap and stop you
> writing.
>
> Every slice must get a full week. Slicing into the same near expiry was measured and
> fails: the late-week writes are one and two day contracts paying almost nothing.

third is always about a week away and the book holds a rotation of dates.

| write on | third expiry lands | days |
|---|---|---|
| Monday | next Monday | 7 |
| Wednesday | next Wednesday | 7 |
| Friday | next Friday | 7 |

> Replaces "the first Friday at least 5 days out", which sounds equivalent and is not:
> from a Monday that jumped to a Friday eleven days out, so the tenor swung between 7
> and 11 days by weekday. Measured under the live 15-contract cap:
>
> | expiry | tenor | premium/yr | avg price paid |
> |---|---|---|---|
> | nearest Friday | 4d | $610,986 | -1.8% vs market |
> | **3 expiries out** | 7d | **$879,322** | **-3.3%** |
> | 4 expiries out | 10d | $764,975 | -3.7% |
>
> Better on premium and on entry price at once. Four out buys slightly cheaper but
> gives back $114k, because longer contracts sit in the 15-contract cap and stop you
> writing.
>
> Every slice must get a full week. Slicing into the same near expiry was measured and
> fails: the late-week writes are one and two day contracts paying almost nothing.

>

> |---|---|---|---|
> | nearest Friday | 4d | $610,986 | -1.8% vs market |
> | **3 expiries out** | 7d | **$879,322** | **-3.3%** |
> | 4 expiries out | 10d | $764,975 | -3.7% |
>
> Better on premium and on entry price at once. Four out buys slightly cheaper but
> gives back $114k, because longer contracts sit in the 15-contract cap and stop you
> writing.

> fails: the late-week writes are one and two day contracts paying almost nothing.

>
> | expiry | tenor | premium/yr | avg price paid |
> |---|---|---|---|
> | nearest Friday | 4d | $610,986 | -1.8% vs market |
> | **3 expiries out** | 7d | **$879,322** | **-3.3%** |
> | 4 expiries out | 10d | $764,975 | -3.7% |
>
> Better on premium and on entry price at once. Four out buys slightly cheaper but
> gives back $114k, because longer contracts sit in the 15-contract cap and stop you
> writing.
>
> Every slice must get a full week. Slicing into the same near expiry was measured and
> fails: the late-week writes are one and two day contracts paying almost nothing.

third is always about a week away and the book holds a rotation of dates.

| write on | third expiry lands | days |
|---|---|---|
| Monday | next Monday | 7 |
| Wednesday | next Wednesday | 7 |
| Friday | next Friday | 7 |

> Replaces "the first Friday at least 5 days out", which sounds equivalent and is not:
> from a Monday that jumped to a Friday eleven days out, so the tenor swung between 7
> and 11 days by weekday. Measured under the live 15-contract cap:
>
> | expiry | tenor | premium/yr | avg price paid |
> |---|---|---|---|
> | nearest Friday | 4d | $610,986 | -1.8% vs market |
> | **3 expiries out** | 7d | **$879,322** | **-3.3%** |
> | 4 expiries out | 10d | $764,975 | -3.7% |
>
> Better on premium and on entry price at once. Four out buys slightly cheaper but
> gives back $114k, because longer contracts sit in the 15-contract cap and stop you
> writing.
>
> Every slice must get a full week. Slicing into the same near expiry was measured and
> fails: the late-week writes are one and two day contracts paying almost nothing.

| Friday | next Friday | 7 |

> Replaces "the first Friday at least 5 days out", which sounds equivalent and is not:
> from a Monday that jumped to a Friday eleven days out, so the tenor swung between 7
> and 11 days by weekday. Measured under the live 15-contract cap:
>
> | expiry | tenor | premium/yr | avg price paid |
> |---|---|---|---|
> | nearest Friday | 4d | $610,986 | -1.8% vs market |
> | **3 expiries out** | 7d | **$879,322** | **-3.3%** |
> | 4 expiries out | 10d | $764,975 | -3.7% |
>
> Better on premium and on entry price at once. Four out buys slightly cheaper but
> gives back $114k, because longer contracts sit in the 15-contract cap and stop you
> writing.
>
> Every slice must get a full week. Slicing into the same near expiry was measured and
> fails: the late-week writes are one and two day contracts paying almost nothing.

>
> | expiry | tenor | premium/yr | avg price paid |
> |---|---|---|---|
> | nearest Friday | 4d | $610,986 | -1.8% vs market |
> | **3 expiries out** | 7d | **$879,322** | **-3.3%** |
> | 4 expiries out | 10d | $764,975 | -3.7% |
>
> Better on premium and on entry price at once. Four out buys slightly cheaper but
> gives back $114k, because longer contracts sit in the 15-contract cap and stop you
> writing.
>
> Every slice must get a full week. Slicing into the same near expiry was measured and
> fails: the late-week writes are one and two day contracts paying almost nothing.

D### What expiry
**The third expiry out**, whatever weekday it falls on. NVDA lists Mon/Wed/Fri, so the
third is always about a week away and the book holds a rotation of dates.

| write on | third expiry lands | days |
|---|---|---|
| Monday | next Monday | 7 |
| Wednesday | next Wednesday | 7 |
| Friday | next Friday | 7 |

> Replaces "the first Friday at least 5 days out", which sounds equivalent and is not:
> from a Monday that jumped to a Friday eleven days out, so the tenor swung between 7
> and 11 days by weekday. Measured under the live 15-contract cap:
>
> | expiry | tenor | premium/yr | avg price paid |
> |---|---|---|---|
> | nearest Friday | 4d | $610,986 | -1.8% vs market |
> | **3 expiries out** | 7d | **$879,322** | **-3.3%** |
> | 4 expiries out | 10d | $764,975 | -3.7% |
>
> Better on premium and on entry price at once. Four out buys slightly cheaper but
> gives back $114k, because longer contracts sit in the 15-contract cap and stop you
> writing.
>
> Every slice must get a full week. Slicing into the same near expiry was measured and
> fails: the late-week writes are one and two day contracts paying almost nothing.

third is always about a week away and the book holds a rotation of dates.

| write on | third expiry lands | days |
|---|---|---|
| Monday | next Monday | 7 |
| Wednesday | next Wednesday | 7 |
| Friday | next Friday | 7 |

> Replaces "the first Friday at least 5 days out", which sounds equivalent and is not:
> from a Monday that jumped to a Friday eleven days out, so the tenor swung between 7
> and 11 days by weekday. Measured under the live 15-contract cap:
>
> | expiry | tenor | premium/yr | avg price paid |
> |---|---|---|---|
> | nearest Friday | 4d | $610,986 | -1.8% vs market |
> | **3 expiries out** | 7d | **$879,322** | **-3.3%** |
> | 4 expiries out | 10d | $764,975 | -3.7% |
>
> Better on premium and on entry price at once. Four out buys slightly cheaper but
> gives back $114k, because longer contracts sit in the 15-contract cap and stop you
> writing.
>
> Every slice must get a full week. Slicing into the same near expiry was measured and
> fails: the late-week writes are one and two day contracts paying almost nothing.

| Friday | next Friday | 7 |

> Replaces "the first Friday at least 5 days out", which sounds equivalent and is not:
> from a Monday that jumped to a Friday eleven days out, so the tenor swung between 7
> and 11 days by weekday. Measured under the live 15-contract cap:
>
> | expiry | tenor | premium/yr | avg price paid |
> |---|---|---|---|
> | nearest Friday | 4d | $610,986 | -1.8% vs market |
> | **3 expiries out** | 7d | **$879,322** | **-3.3%** |
> | 4 expiries out | 10d | $764,975 | -3.7% |
>
> Better on premium and on entry price at once. Four out buys slightly cheaper but
> gives back $114k, because longer contracts sit in the 15-contract cap and stop you
> writing.
>
> Every slice must get a full week. Slicing into the same near expiry was measured and
> fails: the late-week writes are one and two day contracts paying almost nothing.

>
> | expiry | tenor | premium/yr | avg price paid |
> |---|---|---|---|
> | nearest Friday | 4d | $610,986 | -1.8% vs market |
> | **3 expiries out** | 7d | **$879,322** | **-3.3%** |
> | 4 expiries out | 10d | $764,975 | -3.7% |
>
> Better on premium and on entry price at once. Four out buys slightly cheaper but
> gives back $114k, because longer contracts sit in the 15-contract cap and stop you
> writing.
>
> Every slice must get a full week. Slicing into the same near expiry was measured and
> fails: the late-week writes are one and two day contracts paying almost nothing.

c### What expiry
**The third expiry out**, whatever weekday it falls on. NVDA lists Mon/Wed/Fri, so the
third is always about a week away and the book holds a rotation of dates.

| write on | third expiry lands | days |
|---|---|---|
| Monday | next Monday | 7 |
| Wednesday | next Wednesday | 7 |
| Friday | next Friday | 7 |

> Replaces "the first Friday at least 5 days out", which sounds equivalent and is not:
> from a Monday that jumped to a Friday eleven days out, so the tenor swung between 7
> and 11 days by weekday. Measured under the live 15-contract cap:
>
> | expiry | tenor | premium/yr | avg price paid |
> |---|---|---|---|
> | nearest Friday | 4d | $610,986 | -1.8% vs market |
> | **3 expiries out** | 7d | **$879,322** | **-3.3%** |
> | 4 expiries out | 10d | $764,975 | -3.7% |
>
> Better on premium and on entry price at once. Four out buys slightly cheaper but
> gives back $114k, because longer contracts sit in the 15-contract cap and stop you
> writing.
>
> Every slice must get a full week. Slicing into the same near expiry was measured and
> fails: the late-week writes are one and two day contracts paying almost nothing.

third is always about a week away and the book holds a rotation of dates.

| write on | third expiry lands | days |
|---|---|---|
| Monday | next Monday | 7 |
| Wednesday | next Wednesday | 7 |
| Friday | next Friday | 7 |

> Replaces "the first Friday at least 5 days out", which sounds equivalent and is not:
> from a Monday that jumped to a Friday eleven days out, so the tenor swung between 7
> and 11 days by weekday. Measured under the live 15-contract cap:
>
> | expiry | tenor | premium/yr | avg price paid |
> |---|---|---|---|
> | nearest Friday | 4d | $610,986 | -1.8% vs market |
> | **3 expiries out** | 7d | **$879,322** | **-3.3%** |
> | 4 expiries out | 10d | $764,975 | -3.7% |
>
> Better on premium and on entry price at once. Four out buys slightly cheaper but
> gives back $114k, because longer contracts sit in the 15-contract cap and stop you
> writing.
>
> Every slice must get a full week. Slicing into the same near expiry was measured and
> fails: the late-week writes are one and two day contracts paying almost nothing.

| Friday | next Friday | 7 |

> Replaces "the first Friday at least 5 days out", which sounds equivalent and is not:
> from a Monday that jumped to a Friday eleven days out, so the tenor swung between 7
> and 11 days by weekday. Measured under the live 15-contract cap:
>
> | expiry | tenor | premium/yr | avg price paid |
> |---|---|---|---|
> | nearest Friday | 4d | $610,986 | -1.8% vs market |
> | **3 expiries out** | 7d | **$879,322** | **-3.3%** |
> | 4 expiries out | 10d | $764,975 | -3.7% |
>
> Better on premium and on entry price at once. Four out buys slightly cheaper but
> gives back $114k, because longer contracts sit in the 15-contract cap and stop you
> writing.
>
> Every slice must get a full week. Slicing into the same near expiry was measured and
> fails: the late-week writes are one and two day contracts paying almost nothing.

>
> | expiry | tenor | premium/yr | avg price paid |
> |---|---|---|---|
> | nearest Friday | 4d | $610,986 | -1.8% vs market |
> | **3 expiries out** | 7d | **$879,322** | **-3.3%** |
> | 4 expiries out | 10d | $764,975 | -3.7% |
>
> Better on premium and on entry price at once. Four out buys slightly cheaper but
> gives back $114k, because longer contracts sit in the 15-contract cap and stop you
> writing.
>
> Every slice must get a full week. Slicing into the same near expiry was measured and
> fails: the late-week writes are one and two day contracts paying almost nothing.

>

>
> Better on premium and on entry price at once. Four out buys slightly cheaper but
> gives back $114k, because longer contracts sit in the 15-contract cap and stop you
> writing.

> fails: the late-week writes are one and two day contracts paying almost nothing.

third is always about a week away and the book holds a rotation of dates.

| write on | third expiry lands | days |
|---|---|---|
| Monday | next Monday | 7 |
| Wednesday | next Wednesday | 7 |
| Friday | next Friday | 7 |

> Replaces "the first Friday at least 5 days out", which sounds equivalent and is not:
> from a Monday that jumped to a Friday eleven days out, so the tenor swung between 7
> and 11 days by weekday. Measured under the live 15-contract cap:
>
> | expiry | tenor | premium/yr | avg price paid |
> |---|---|---|---|
> | nearest Friday | 4d | $610,986 | -1.8% vs market |
> | **3 expiries out** | 7d | **$879,322** | **-3.3%** |
> | 4 expiries out | 10d | $764,975 | -3.7% |
>
> Better on premium and on entry price at once. Four out buys slightly cheaper but
> gives back $114k, because longer contracts sit in the 15-contract cap and stop you
> writing.
>
> Every slice must get a full week. Slicing into the same near expiry was measured and
> fails: the late-week writes are one and two day contracts paying almost nothing.

| Friday | next Friday | 7 |

> Replaces "the first Friday at least 5 days out", which sounds equivalent and is not:
> from a Monday that jumped to a Friday eleven days out, so the tenor swung between 7
> and 11 days by weekday. Measured under the live 15-contract cap:
>
> | expiry | tenor | premium/yr | avg price paid |
> |---|---|---|---|
> | nearest Friday | 4d | $610,986 | -1.8% vs market |
> | **3 expiries out** | 7d | **$879,322** | **-3.3%** |
> | 4 expiries out | 10d | $764,975 | -3.7% |
>
> Better on premium and on entry price at once. Four out buys slightly cheaper but
> gives back $114k, because longer contracts sit in the 15-contract cap and stop you
> writing.
>
> Every slice must get a full week. Slicing into the same near expiry was measured and
> fails: the late-week writes are one and two day contracts paying almost nothing.

>
> | expiry | tenor | premium/yr | avg price paid |
> |---|---|---|---|
> | nearest Friday | 4d | $610,986 | -1.8% vs market |
> | **3 expiries out** | 7d | **$879,322** | **-3.3%** |
> | 4 expiries out | 10d | $764,975 | -3.7% |
>
> Better on premium and on entry price at once. Four out buys slightly cheaper but
> gives back $114k, because longer contracts sit in the 15-contract cap and stop you
> writing.
>
> Every slice must get a full week. Slicing into the same near expiry was measured and
> fails: the late-week writes are one and two day contracts paying almost nothing.

**The third expiry out**, whatever weekday it falls on. NVDA lists Mon/Wed/Fri, so the

| write on | third expiry lands | days |
|---|---|---|

| Wednesday | next Wednesday | 7 |
| Friday | next Friday | 7 |

> Replaces "the first Friday at least 5 days out", which sounds equivalent and is not:
> from a Monday that jumped to a Friday eleven days out, so the tenor swung between 7
> and 11 days by weekday. Measured under the live 15-contract cap:
>
> | expiry | tenor | premium/yr | avg price paid |
> |---|---|---|---|

> | **3 expiries out** | 7d | **$879,322** | **-3.3%** |
> | 4 expiries out | 10d | $764,975 | -3.7% |
>
> Better on premium and on entry price at once. Four out buys slightly cheaper but
> gives back $114k, because longer contracts sit in the 15-contract cap and stop you
> writing.
>
> Every slice must get a full week. Slicing into the same near expiry was measured and
> fails: the late-week writes are one and two day contracts paying almost nothing.

third is always about a week away and the book holds a rotation of dates.

| write on | third expiry lands | days |
|---|---|---|
| Monday | next Monday | 7 |
| Wednesday | next Wednesday | 7 |
| Friday | next Friday | 7 |

> Replaces "the first Friday at least 5 days out", which sounds equivalent and is not:
> from a Monday that jumped to a Friday eleven days out, so the tenor swung between 7
> and 11 days by weekday. Measured under the live 15-contract cap:
>
> | expiry | tenor | premium/yr | avg price paid |
> |---|---|---|---|
> | nearest Friday | 4d | $610,986 | -1.8% vs market |
> | **3 expiries out** | 7d | **$879,322** | **-3.3%** |
> | 4 expiries out | 10d | $764,975 | -3.7% |
>
> Better on premium and on entry price at once. Four out buys slightly cheaper but
> gives back $114k, because longer contracts sit in the 15-contract cap and stop you
> writing.
>
> Every slice must get a full week. Slicing into the same near expiry was measured and
> fails: the late-week writes are one and two day contracts paying almost nothing.

| Friday | next Friday | 7 |

> Replaces "the first Friday at least 5 days out", which sounds equivalent and is not:
> from a Monday that jumped to a Friday eleven days out, so the tenor swung between 7
> and 11 days by weekday. Measured under the live 15-contract cap:
>
> | expiry | tenor | premium/yr | avg price paid |
> |---|---|---|---|
> | nearest Friday | 4d | $610,986 | -1.8% vs market |
> | **3 expiries out** | 7d | **$879,322** | **-3.3%** |
> | 4 expiries out | 10d | $764,975 | -3.7% |
>
> Better on premium and on entry price at once. Four out buys slightly cheaper but
> gives back $114k, because longer contracts sit in the 15-contract cap and stop you
> writing.
>
> Every slice must get a full week. Slicing into the same near expiry was measured and
> fails: the late-week writes are one and two day contracts paying almost nothing.

>
> | expiry | tenor | premium/yr | avg price paid |
> |---|---|---|---|
> | nearest Friday | 4d | $610,986 | -1.8% vs market |
> | **3 expiries out** | 7d | **$879,322** | **-3.3%** |
> | 4 expiries out | 10d | $764,975 | -3.7% |
>
> Better on premium and on entry price at once. Four out buys slightly cheaper but
> gives back $114k, because longer contracts sit in the 15-contract cap and stop you
> writing.
>
> Every slice must get a full week. Slicing into the same near expiry was measured and
> fails: the late-week writes are one and two day contracts paying almost nothing.

**The third expiry out**, whatever weekday it falls on. NVDA lists Mon/Wed/Fri, so the
third is always about a week away and the book holds a rotation of dates.

| write on | third expiry lands | days |
|---|---|---|
| Monday | next Monday | 7 |
| Wednesday | next Wednesday | 7 |
| Friday | next Friday | 7 |

> Replaces "the first Friday at least 5 days out", which sounds equivalent and is not:
> from a Monday that jumped to a Friday eleven days out, so the tenor swung between 7
> and 11 days by weekday. Measured under the live 15-contract cap:
>
> | expiry | tenor | premium/yr | avg price paid |
> |---|---|---|---|

> | **3 expiries out** | 7d | **$879,322** | **-3.3%** |
> | 4 expiries out | 10d | $764,975 | -3.7% |
>
> Better on premium and on entry price at once. Four out buys slightly cheaper but
> gives back $114k, because longer contracts sit in the 15-contract cap and stop you
> writing.
>
> Every slice must get a full week. Slicing into the same near expiry was measured and
> fails: the late-week writes are one and two day contracts paying almost nothing.

third is always about a week away and the book holds a rotation of dates.

| write on | third expiry lands | days |
|---|---|---|
| Monday | next Monday | 7 |
| Wednesday | next Wednesday | 7 |
| Friday | next Friday | 7 |

> Replaces "the first Friday at least 5 days out", which sounds equivalent and is not:
> from a Monday that jumped to a Friday eleven days out, so the tenor swung between 7
> and 11 days by weekday. Measured under the live 15-contract cap:
>
> | expiry | tenor | premium/yr | avg price paid |
> |---|---|---|---|
> | nearest Friday | 4d | $610,986 | -1.8% vs market |
> | **3 expiries out** | 7d | **$879,322** | **-3.3%** |
> | 4 expiries out | 10d | $764,975 | -3.7% |
>
> Better on premium and on entry price at once. Four out buys slightly cheaper but
> gives back $114k, because longer contracts sit in the 15-contract cap and stop you
> writing.
>
> Every slice must get a full week. Slicing into the same near expiry was measured and
> fails: the late-week writes are one and two day contracts paying almost nothing.

| Friday | next Friday | 7 |

> Replaces "the first Friday at least 5 days out", which sounds equivalent and is not:
> from a Monday that jumped to a Friday eleven days out, so the tenor swung between 7
> and 11 days by weekday. Measured under the live 15-contract cap:
>
> | expiry | tenor | premium/yr | avg price paid |
> |---|---|---|---|
> | nearest Friday | 4d | $610,986 | -1.8% vs market |
> | **3 expiries out** | 7d | **$879,322** | **-3.3%** |
> | 4 expiries out | 10d | $764,975 | -3.7% |
>
> Better on premium and on entry price at once. Four out buys slightly cheaper but
> gives back $114k, because longer contracts sit in the 15-contract cap and stop you
> writing.
>
> Every slice must get a full week. Slicing into the same near expiry was measured and
> fails: the late-week writes are one and two day contracts paying almost nothing.

> writing.

**The third expiry out**, whatever weekday it falls on. NVDA lists Mon/Wed/Fri, so the
third is always about a week away and the book holds a rotation of dates.

| write on | third expiry lands | days |
|---|---|---|
| Monday | next Monday | 7 |
| Wednesday | next Wednesday | 7 |
| Friday | next Friday | 7 |

> Replaces "the first Friday at least 5 days out", which sounds equivalent and is not:
> from a Monday that jumped to a Friday eleven days out, so the tenor swung between 7
> and 11 days by weekday. Measured under the live 15-contract cap:
>
> | expiry | tenor | premium/yr | avg price paid |
> |---|---|---|---|
> | nearest Friday | 4d | $610,986 | -1.8% vs market |
> | **3 expiries out** | 7d | **$879,322** | **-3.3%** |
> | 4 expiries out | 10d | $764,975 | -3.7% |
>
> Better on premium and on entry price at once. Four out buys slightly cheaper but
> gives back $114k, because longer contracts sit in the 15-contract cap and stop you
> writing.
>
> Every slice must get a full week. Slicing into the same near expiry was measured and
> fails: the late-week writes are one and two day contracts paying almost nothing.

third is always about a week away and the book holds a rotation of dates.

| write on | third expiry lands | days |
|---|---|---|
| Monday | next Monday | 7 |
| Wednesday | next Wednesday | 7 |
| Friday | next Friday | 7 |

> Replaces "the first Friday at least 5 days out", which sounds equivalent and is not:
> from a Monday that jumped to a Friday eleven days out, so the tenor swung between 7
> and 11 days by weekday. Measured under the live 15-contract cap:
>
> | expiry | tenor | premium/yr | avg price paid |
> |---|---|---|---|
> | nearest Friday | 4d | $610,986 | -1.8% vs market |
> | **3 expiries out** | 7d | **$879,322** | **-3.3%** |
> | 4 expiries out | 10d | $764,975 | -3.7% |
>
> Better on premium and on entry price at once. Four out buys slightly cheaper but
> gives back $114k, because longer contracts sit in the 15-contract cap and stop you
> writing.
>
> Every slice must get a full week. Slicing into the same near expiry was measured and
> fails: the late-week writes are one and two day contracts paying almost nothing.

> | **3 expiries out** | 7d | **$879,322** | **-3.3%** |
> | 4 expiries out | 10d | $764,975 | -3.7% |
>
> Better on premium and on entry price at once. Four out buys slightly cheaper but

> writing.

> fails: the late-week writes are one and two day contracts paying almost nothing.

> gives back $114k, because longer contracts sit in the 15-contract cap and stop you
> writing.

third is always about a week away and the book holds a rotation of dates.

| write on | third expiry lands | days |
|---|---|---|
| Monday | next Monday | 7 |
| Wednesday | next Wednesday | 7 |
| Friday | next Friday | 7 |

> Replaces "the first Friday at least 5 days out", which sounds equivalent and is not:
> from a Monday that jumped to a Friday eleven days out, so the tenor swung between 7
> and 11 days by weekday. Measured under the live 15-contract cap:
>
> | expiry | tenor | premium/yr | avg price paid |
> |---|---|---|---|
> | nearest Friday | 4d | $610,986 | -1.8% vs market |
> | **3 expiries out** | 7d | **$879,322** | **-3.3%** |
> | 4 expiries out | 10d | $764,975 | -3.7% |
>
> Better on premium and on entry price at once. Four out buys slightly cheaper but
> gives back $114k, because longer contracts sit in the 15-contract cap and stop you
> writing.
>
> Every slice must get a full week. Slicing into the same near expiry was measured and
> fails: the late-week writes are one and two day contracts paying almost nothing.

| Friday | next Friday | 7 |

> Replaces "the first Friday at least 5 days out", which sounds equivalent and is not:
> from a Monday that jumped to a Friday eleven days out, so the tenor swung between 7
> and 11 days by weekday. Measured under the live 15-contract cap:
>
> | expiry | tenor | premium/yr | avg price paid |
> |---|---|---|---|
> | nearest Friday | 4d | $610,986 | -1.8% vs market |
> | **3 expiries out** | 7d | **$879,322** | **-3.3%** |
> | 4 expiries out | 10d | $764,975 | -3.7% |
>
> Better on premium and on entry price at once. Four out buys slightly cheaper but
> gives back $114k, because longer contracts sit in the 15-contract cap and stop you
> writing.
>
> Every slice must get a full week. Slicing into the same near expiry was measured and
> fails: the late-week writes are one and two day contracts paying almost nothing.

> | **3 expiries out** | 7d | **$879,322** | **-3.3%** |
> | 4 expiries out | 10d | $764,975 | -3.7% |
>
> Better on premium and on entry price at once. Four out buys slightly cheaper but
> gives back $114k, because longer contracts sit in the 15-contract cap and stop you
> writing.
>
> Every slice must get a full week. Slicing into the same near expiry was measured and
> fails: the late-week writes are one and two day contracts paying almost nothing.

third is always about a week away and the book holds a rotation of dates.

| write on | third expiry lands | days |
|---|---|---|
| Monday | next Monday | 7 |
| Wednesday | next Wednesday | 7 |
| Friday | next Friday | 7 |

> Replaces "the first Friday at least 5 days out", which sounds equivalent and is not:
> from a Monday that jumped to a Friday eleven days out, so the tenor swung between 7
> and 11 days by weekday. Measured under the live 15-contract cap:
>
> | expiry | tenor | premium/yr | avg price paid |
> |---|---|---|---|
> | nearest Friday | 4d | $610,986 | -1.8% vs market |
> | **3 expiries out** | 7d | **$879,322** | **-3.3%** |
> | 4 expiries out | 10d | $764,975 | -3.7% |
>
> Better on premium and on entry price at once. Four out buys slightly cheaper but
> gives back $114k, because longer contracts sit in the 15-contract cap and stop you
> writing.
>
> Every slice must get a full week. Slicing into the same near expiry was measured and
> fails: the late-week writes are one and two day contracts paying almost nothing.

| Friday | next Friday | 7 |

> Replaces "the first Friday at least 5 days out", which sounds equivalent and is not:
> from a Monday that jumped to a Friday eleven days out, so the tenor swung between 7
> and 11 days by weekday. Measured under the live 15-contract cap:
>
> | expiry | tenor | premium/yr | avg price paid |
> |---|---|---|---|
> | nearest Friday | 4d | $610,986 | -1.8% vs market |
> | **3 expiries out** | 7d | **$879,322** | **-3.3%** |
> | 4 expiries out | 10d | $764,975 | -3.7% |
>
> Better on premium and on entry price at once. Four out buys slightly cheaper but
> gives back $114k, because longer contracts sit in the 15-contract cap and stop you
> writing.
>
> Every slice must get a full week. Slicing into the same near expiry was measured and
> fails: the late-week writes are one and two day contracts paying almost nothing.

>
> | expiry | tenor | premium/yr | avg price paid |
> |---|---|---|---|
> | nearest Friday | 4d | $610,986 | -1.8% vs market |
> | **3 expiries out** | 7d | **$879,322** | **-3.3%** |
> | 4 expiries out | 10d | $764,975 | -3.7% |
>
> Better on premium and on entry price at once. Four out buys slightly cheaper but
> gives back $114k, because longer contracts sit in the 15-contract cap and stop you
> writing.
>
> Every slice must get a full week. Slicing into the same near expiry was measured and
> fails: the late-week writes are one and two day contracts paying almost nothing.

l### What expiry
**The third expiry out**, whatever weekday it falls on. NVDA lists Mon/Wed/Fri, so the
third is always about a week away and the book holds a rotation of dates.

| write on | third expiry lands | days |
|---|---|---|
| Monday | next Monday | 7 |
| Wednesday | next Wednesday | 7 |
| Friday | next Friday | 7 |

> Replaces "the first Friday at least 5 days out", which sounds equivalent and is not:
> from a Monday that jumped to a Friday eleven days out, so the tenor swung between 7
> and 11 days by weekday. Measured under the live 15-contract cap:
>
> | expiry | tenor | premium/yr | avg price paid |
> |---|---|---|---|
> | nearest Friday | 4d | $610,986 | -1.8% vs market |
> | **3 expiries out** | 7d | **$879,322** | **-3.3%** |
> | 4 expiries out | 10d | $764,975 | -3.7% |
>
> Better on premium and on entry price at once. Four out buys slightly cheaper but
> gives back $114k, because longer contracts sit in the 15-contract cap and stop you
> writing.
>
> Every slice must get a full week. Slicing into the same near expiry was measured and
> fails: the late-week writes are one and two day contracts paying almost nothing.

third is always about a week away and the book holds a rotation of dates.

| write on | third expiry lands | days |
|---|---|---|
| Monday | next Monday | 7 |
| Wednesday | next Wednesday | 7 |
| Friday | next Friday | 7 |

> Replaces "the first Friday at least 5 days out", which sounds equivalent and is not:
> from a Monday that jumped to a Friday eleven days out, so the tenor swung between 7
> and 11 days by weekday. Measured under the live 15-contract cap:
>
> | expiry | tenor | premium/yr | avg price paid |
> |---|---|---|---|
> | nearest Friday | 4d | $610,986 | -1.8% vs market |
> | **3 expiries out** | 7d | **$879,322** | **-3.3%** |
> | 4 expiries out | 10d | $764,975 | -3.7% |
>
> Better on premium and on entry price at once. Four out buys slightly cheaper but
> gives back $114k, because longer contracts sit in the 15-contract cap and stop you
> writing.
>
> Every slice must get a full week. Slicing into the same near expiry was measured and
> fails: the late-week writes are one and two day contracts paying almost nothing.

| Friday | next Friday | 7 |

> Replaces "the first Friday at least 5 days out", which sounds equivalent and is not:
> from a Monday that jumped to a Friday eleven days out, so the tenor swung between 7
> and 11 days by weekday. Measured under the live 15-contract cap:
>
> | expiry | tenor | premium/yr | avg price paid |
> |---|---|---|---|
> | nearest Friday | 4d | $610,986 | -1.8% vs market |
> | **3 expiries out** | 7d | **$879,322** | **-3.3%** |
> | 4 expiries out | 10d | $764,975 | -3.7% |
>
> Better on premium and on entry price at once. Four out buys slightly cheaper but
> gives back $114k, because longer contracts sit in the 15-contract cap and stop you
> writing.
>
> Every slice must get a full week. Slicing into the same near expiry was measured and
> fails: the late-week writes are one and two day contracts paying almost nothing.

**The third expiry out**, whatever weekday it falls on. NVDA lists Mon/Wed/Fri, so the
third is always about a week away and the book holds a rotation of dates.

| write on | third expiry lands | days |
|---|---|---|

| Wednesday | next Wednesday | 7 |
| Friday | next Friday | 7 |

> Replaces "the first Friday at least 5 days out", which sounds equivalent and is not:
> from a Monday that jumped to a Friday eleven days out, so the tenor swung between 7
> and 11 days by weekday. Measured under the live 15-contract cap:
>

> | **3 expiries out** | 7d | **$879,322** | **-3.3%** |
> | 4 expiries out | 10d | $764,975 | -3.7% |
>
> Better on premium and on entry price at once. Four out buys slightly cheaper but
> gives back $114k, because longer contracts sit in the 15-contract cap and stop you
> writing.
>
> Every slice must get a full week. Slicing into the same near expiry was measured and
> fails: the late-week writes are one and two day contracts paying almost nothing.

third is always about a week away and the book holds a rotation of dates.

| write on | third expiry lands | days |
|---|---|---|
| Monday | next Monday | 7 |
| Wednesday | next Wednesday | 7 |
| Friday | next Friday | 7 |

> Replaces "the first Friday at least 5 days out", which sounds equivalent and is not:
> from a Monday that jumped to a Friday eleven days out, so the tenor swung between 7
> and 11 days by weekday. Measured under the live 15-contract cap:
>
> | expiry | tenor | premium/yr | avg price paid |
> |---|---|---|---|
> | nearest Friday | 4d | $610,986 | -1.8% vs market |
> | **3 expiries out** | 7d | **$879,322** | **-3.3%** |
> | 4 expiries out | 10d | $764,975 | -3.7% |
>
> Better on premium and on entry price at once. Four out buys slightly cheaper but
> gives back $114k, because longer contracts sit in the 15-contract cap and stop you
> writing.
>
> Every slice must get a full week. Slicing into the same near expiry was measured and
> fails: the late-week writes are one and two day contracts paying almost nothing.

| Friday | next Friday | 7 |

> Replaces "the first Friday at least 5 days out", which sounds equivalent and is not:
> from a Monday that jumped to a Friday eleven days out, so the tenor swung between 7
> and 11 days by weekday. Measured under the live 15-contract cap:
>
> | expiry | tenor | premium/yr | avg price paid |
> |---|---|---|---|
> | nearest Friday | 4d | $610,986 | -1.8% vs market |
> | **3 expiries out** | 7d | **$879,322** | **-3.3%** |
> | 4 expiries out | 10d | $764,975 | -3.7% |
>
> Better on premium and on entry price at once. Four out buys slightly cheaper but
> gives back $114k, because longer contracts sit in the 15-contract cap and stop you
> writing.
>
> Every slice must get a full week. Slicing into the same near expiry was measured and
> fails: the late-week writes are one and two day contracts paying almost nothing.

>
> | expiry | tenor | premium/yr | avg price paid |
> |---|---|---|---|
> | nearest Friday | 4d | $610,986 | -1.8% vs market |
> | **3 expiries out** | 7d | **$879,322** | **-3.3%** |
> | 4 expiries out | 10d | $764,975 | -3.7% |
>
> Better on premium and on entry price at once. Four out buys slightly cheaper but
> gives back $114k, because longer contracts sit in the 15-contract cap and stop you
> writing.
>
> Every slice must get a full week. Slicing into the same near expiry was measured and
> fails: the late-week writes are one and two day contracts paying almost nothing.

e### What expiry
**The third expiry out**, whatever weekday it falls on. NVDA lists Mon/Wed/Fri, so the
third is always about a week away and the book holds a rotation of dates.

| write on | third expiry lands | days |
|---|---|---|
| Monday | next Monday | 7 |
| Wednesday | next Wednesday | 7 |
| Friday | next Friday | 7 |

> Replaces "the first Friday at least 5 days out", which sounds equivalent and is not:
> from a Monday that jumped to a Friday eleven days out, so the tenor swung between 7
> and 11 days by weekday. Measured under the live 15-contract cap:
>
> | expiry | tenor | premium/yr | avg price paid |
> |---|---|---|---|
> | nearest Friday | 4d | $610,986 | -1.8% vs market |
> | **3 expiries out** | 7d | **$879,322** | **-3.3%** |
> | 4 expiries out | 10d | $764,975 | -3.7% |
>
> Better on premium and on entry price at once. Four out buys slightly cheaper but
> gives back $114k, because longer contracts sit in the 15-contract cap and stop you
> writing.
>
> Every slice must get a full week. Slicing into the same near expiry was measured and
> fails: the late-week writes are one and two day contracts paying almost nothing.

third is always about a week away and the book holds a rotation of dates.

| write on | third expiry lands | days |
|---|---|---|
| Monday | next Monday | 7 |
| Wednesday | next Wednesday | 7 |
| Friday | next Friday | 7 |

> Replaces "the first Friday at least 5 days out", which sounds equivalent and is not:
> from a Monday that jumped to a Friday eleven days out, so the tenor swung between 7
> and 11 days by weekday. Measured under the live 15-contract cap:
>
> | expiry | tenor | premium/yr | avg price paid |
> |---|---|---|---|
> | nearest Friday | 4d | $610,986 | -1.8% vs market |
> | **3 expiries out** | 7d | **$879,322** | **-3.3%** |
> | 4 expiries out | 10d | $764,975 | -3.7% |
>
> Better on premium and on entry price at once. Four out buys slightly cheaper but
> gives back $114k, because longer contracts sit in the 15-contract cap and stop you
> writing.
>
> Every slice must get a full week. Slicing into the same near expiry was measured and
> fails: the late-week writes are one and two day contracts paying almost nothing.
